name: Nicolas
overview: Nicolas was a male proselyte from Antioch who was chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jewish believers. His selection highlights the early church's commitment to caring for vulnerable members within the community, particularly those of Hellenistic background. Scripture identifies him specifically for this role, emphasizing his service and dedication.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Nicolas' is the only recorded proper name for this individual, with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated in the biblical text. It is presented plainly without additional titles or meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Nicolas beyond his role among the Hellenistic widows. There are no further relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Nicolas holds significance in the New Testament as one of the seven men chosen to assist in the practical ministry of the early church, specifically to care for widows from the Hellenistic Jewish community. His selection reflects the early church's organized approach to serving its members and maintaining unity between Jewish and Hellenistic believers. Being a proselyte from Antioch, Nicolas also represents the inclusive nature of the early Christian community.
